diseaseDetection.title: Rice Plant Nutritional Deficiencies
diseaseDetection.subtitle: Learn to identify and treat common nutritional deficiencies in rice plants
diseaseDetection.aiNote: Below you'll find comprehensive information about common nutritional deficiencies and their treatments. AI-powered disease detection coming soon.

sulfur.name: Sulfur (S) Deficiency
symptoms: Uniform light green to yellow color (whole plant)
Younger leaves more affected than old
visualSigns: Similar to nitrogen but affects young leaves
prevention: Use ammonium sulfate instead of urea
sulfur.timing: Apply at first symptoms or as preventive measure

symptoms: Uniform yellowing (chlorosis) starting from older leaf tips
Light green to yellow older leaves
visualSigns: Pale yellow-green coloration of entire plant
V-shaped yellowing pattern from leaf tips
treatment: Split application: 50% basal, 25% tillering, 25% panicle initiation
Use ammonium sulfate (21-0-0) for quick results
Foliar spray of 2% urea solution for quick greening
prevention: Apply compost or FYM at 5-10 tons/acre
Avoid over-irrigation that causes nitrogen leaching
nitrogen.timing: Apply immediately at first signs. Response visible in 7-10 days

symptoms: Yellow-orange discoloration starting from older leaf tips
Leaf margins turn yellowish-brown and dry up (firing)
Poor grain filling and small grains
Dark brown necrotic spots on leaves
visualSigns: Brown scorched appearance on leaf margins
Symptoms start from tips and edges
Stems become weak and break easily
treatment: Apply muriate of potash (KCl) at 15-20 kg/acre
Use potassium sulfate for saline soils
Split application: 50% basal, 50% at panicle initiation
prevention: Maintain K:N ratio of 1:1 or higher
potassium.timing: Critical at tillering and flowering stages

symptoms: Purple coloration may appear on leaves
visualSigns: Purplish tint on leaves and stems
causes: Acidic or alkaline soils fixing phosphorus
treatment: Apply rock phosphate in acidic soils
Use water-soluble phosphorus for quick action
phosphorus.timing: Best as basal application before transplanting

symptoms: Dusty brown spots or blotches on older leaves
Chlorosis (whitening) of mid-veins in younger leaves
visualSigns: Brown rusty spots on lower leaves
Plants fail to recover after transplanting shock
treatment: Foliar spray of 0.5% zinc sulfate + 0.25% lime
prevention: Apply zinc every 2-3 years in deficient areas
zinc.timing: Apply before transplanting or at first symptoms

symptoms: Small brown spots on leaves that coalesce
Bronzed or rusty appearance of foliage
Leaf tips and margins turn brown
visualSigns: Purple or reddish tinge on leaves
Extensive leaf area covered with spots
causes: High organic matter in acidic soil
Reduction of ferric to ferrous iron
treatment: Intermittent irrigation instead of continuous flooding
Apply lime to raise pH to 6.0-6.5
prevention: Apply lime before planting in acidic soils
Incorporate rice straw to increase pH
Plant tolerant varieties in problem areas
ironToxicity.timing: Drainage and lime application before symptoms worsen
